sentences.text: Camera.
There we go.
Pretty good.
How are you doing?
Yeah, good, thank you.
This meeting is being recorded.
Good to see you.
Yeah, good to see you again.
How's the, the last few weeks been good?
Pretty good, Pretty good.
Can't complain.
Can't complain.
We've been running the business as usual, but at the same time we've been selling more and more of the new side of the business.
So I think this is part of the, this is going to be part of the conversation today.
Not sure if you want to jump right into it, but I can give you some context just so we can better understand how things are going.
Yeah, sure.
Yeah.
So tell me how this other business fits into what it is that you're doing and what the strategy is.
Sure.
Cool.
So long story short, to give you some context and get you the full picture, we basically have 99 ads.
And on 99 ads, we do Dome for you ads.
So clients need ads, we create the ads, we shoot the ads, we package the ads, they get the ads, they launch the ads and they get the sales.
Now who creates the ads for us is the Creative strategist.
So we have a bunch of creative strategists within our team and they create ads for our clients.
In January, we bought another domain which is creativestrategists.com and basically with creativestrategists.Com what we're doing is place and ramp up creative strategists for clients.
So this is another demographics, another type of audience.
What we recognize is that part of the market doesn't want somebody to create ads for them, but want to create their own in house creative department.
And this is what we help them do.
We're basically recruiting and you can call it consulting, but we're not delivering the ads.
So our thoughts were considering we will be selling 99 ads.
Hopefully there's a way to make it clear up front from the beginning.
We will be more than happy to sign up some sort of exclusivity non compete clause as long as it's narrowed to the delivery of the ads, but not if it includes recruiting, consulting, and so on.
So this is, this is the situation.
Not sure if it's clear.
Happy to add as much context as you might need.
Sorry, I think you froze there for a second or.
I did.
Okay, so.
So you've got the, you've got the, the two different businesses.
How, how developed is this second domain, the Creative Strategists domain?
Is it a new thing or.
Yeah, it's a very new thing.
So the leads that you, you're using for creative strategists.
Are, are they coming out the, the marketing that you're doing for 99 ads?
Are they the same clients or have you just developed a second business on the side?
No, it's literally a second business on the side.
Most of the people are coming through, like my personal brand, So I create YouTube videos and I'm getting people through that, but that's not how we're getting clients for 99 ads.
So there are two different pipelines, basically.
Okay, and so are you, you're hoping to step away from the 99 ads business as soon as possible?
Not as soon as possible, considering that.
I mean, last time we talked about the current ebitda, so we picked it up, we picked it back up and we started optimizing it in January.
So ideally end of the year, that would be where I believe we will be in the best place to sell.

Okay, so are we having this discussion now, but you're, you're planning on selling at the end of the year or did you want to start the process now to get the, the deal done before the end of the year?
So last time we spoke, we mentioned we would have touched base in May to start the preparation so that we could go to market around July, August, I think you mentioned August is usually slow.
So we can start let's say officially in September.
And I mean, I'm guessing three, four months will be more than necessary.
Okay, cool.
So in terms of like the business though, you're happy to sell the business and move on with a non compete business already set up and running?
That's basically what you're saying, and then Francesco will stick around to run 99 ads after the transaction?
Yeah, I think, look, in terms of being able to set up a second business, that's absolutely within your rights.
I don't think it will be a clash.
It looks like a second market, doesn't it?
I mean, it's not the same market.
It's completely secondary.
Yeah, we're going down market, literally because I mean, obviously it's more profitable to sell the recurring six grand a month package.
But there's space down market, which is where we like where we wanted to increase the time.
Just to clarify, Francesco would not be staying in 90 minutes.
Francesco is now part of the delivery, but by the time we sell, we already have another person who's ready to step in.
So as we start the process, we just basically ramp up this person and that should be more than enough.
Okay, cool.
Yeah, I don't see a massive problem with that, particularly if you have the other person already stepping into the leadership role within the business.
I mean, potentially it will always have, it will always have some influence on the valuation if the founders aren't involved.
Because most buyers just want to keep people in for three years.
But we will see.
I mean, that's a conversation we can have.
But the important thing is that we go to market with the plan in place and that we're clear to the buyers that you guys are looking to move on.
So that should, that should deal with it before there is even a question about it.
Okay, cool.

So I've already sent the engagement letter over and obviously as soon as that is signed and we've set everything up and onboarded you, we can get started with the process of putting the valuation together.
If we're looking to wait until September to get started, I mean, August is slow.
The July, July is okay.
But it really depends what you want to do because in terms of like the traction we can get possibly before there is a slowdown, you know, potentially we can get everything up and running.
I mean, I'm just thinking because we've onboarded like six businesses in the last week and there's been a lot of interest with them.
So at the moment, you know, it seems to, the business is really picking up.
You know, it's kind of a spike at the moment.
So it depends on what you guys are looking to do.
But certainly if we started the process now, we would hopefully have everything up and running and a deal done before the end of the year.
So.
My only concern is that.
Basically.
Starting in Jan, we doubled EBITDA compared to the previous year.
So I believe the best, like where is the best situation for us in terms of maximizing the 12 months of trading EBITDA in, hence getting the biggest amount would be end of the year.
But you're the expert, so, so like.
We, obviously, so we, we need to get the, the timing right.
I'm just, just thinking.
So we run a, a really tight six month process and if we can get, if we get the timing right, what will happen is the deal will close within six months, right?
It is kind of.
Sorry, you maybe lost you.
Yeah, I've got a satellite dish.
It's just turned really rubbish just recently this last week.
Is it start.
Sorry, is it startling?
It is, yeah.
Yeah, it is.
I'm getting contrasting opinions.
It's really good.
But I think what's happened is the trees are all grown and it must hit the tree.
Yeah, Sorry.
Where did I, where did I dip Out.
So I'm just thinking on the timing.
Of the six months process.
Yeah.
So if we run a six month process and we get everything up and ready and out as quickly as possible, I think we can maybe enjoy some of this spike that we've, we've currently got going.
And also just, I was just saying at the point where the deal gets done, which will be six months, that would be where the valuation really matters.
So that it's not really now what we would do is we'd value the business on whatever your projection is.
So if you're saying this is how much we're going to be worth by the end of the year based on what our current numbers are, then we can just put that down and work towards it.
And so when we close on that day that we close, that's when really it really counts what the value of the business would look like at that point.
So if you want to get the deal done before the end of the year, then we could get started.
If you don't mind it running into next year and maybe spring or early summer next year to close, then we can get started a bit later in September.
Okay.
Okay.
I think that makes perfect sense.
Especially if we can already consume consider what we expect to be the right numbers by the end of the year.
We're in a good position.
Meaning that we're not running away.
I mean if we get into the next year, the EBITDA is just going to go up hopefully.
But we're in a solid position, I would say.
So it's just a matter of making sure that we are maximizing the, like that trading EBITDA as much as we can.
Yeah, but so, so the important thing is for, for us is to get the valuation done on, on the multiple.
So when we get to, to whenever the, the deal is closing, it's really the mo.
The multiple that we're agreeing on.
So if your EBITDA has gone up and you've performed even better then, then that's absolutely fine.
I mean you will, you'll enjoy the benefits of the hard work.

Yeah, so, and also I think just in terms of buyers they want there's a, there's quite a bad market at the moment where we're trying to, because we work on the buy side as well with our clients trying to buy agencies and they tell us, you know, our number is, is whatever, you know, 5 million or whatever.

And then we get into their finances and actually they're, they're overestimating or they're lying about, you know, They've had a bad year last year and you know, there's quite a lot of underperforming agencies.

So if you can sell while you're still going up, I think there'll be potentially a lot more interest because people can see that you're already riding the wave rather than on the way down, which is where we're seeing a lot.
Yeah, I mean, a lot of agencies just had a bad year last year, but they're not talking about until the last minute, which makes buyers walk away.
You know, they don't, they don't want to hear that.
If you've just been telling them you're doing 5 million and then you're not really, or you've had a really bad 12 months.
So.
So yeah, all of those things to consider.
What, so what are you thinking at the moment?
Which would you prefer to do?
If it takes six months, I'm guessing like the best situation would be starting probably around like end of the month.
So we have six full months again, July, August, not sure how to consider those two months, but still, I mean, we work.
So I'm guessing the main problem is the market and the outreach to potential buyers not working out that well.
But if that speeds up the process and we can get out by end of the year, that would be perfect for us.
Francesco, what do you think?
I think it's good.
That's basically what we discussed previously, so it makes sense.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
All right.
So sorry, Glenn.
Yeah.
Just one question regarding.
So you mentioned that founders getting out would be conducive to a smaller multiplier.
What would be the difference in that case?
I mean, obviously there are a million things to consider, but usually what is the, like the type of difference you see?
So, so really the difference is it can be half a point to a point.
I mean, it's not, it wouldn't be a huge difference.
But say we were, we were shooting for a 5 or a 6X and somebody decided that they didn't like the fact that you were walking then, then potentially they would, they're going to put in lower offers.

But the fact is we want to go to market with the story straight that you guys are not no longer involved in the day to day running and that you have management in place that's already taken over the day to day.
So I mean, what we want to do is create enough interest where it doesn't matter if somebody has given us a lower offer, that we've got a, we've got a higher offer.
I mean it, it really does depend on who the buyer is.
You know, some, some buyers that are owner operators.

So what we, we sometimes see is people that want to buy a business and run it themselves rather than somebody that already has an agency and they're looking to bolt more agencies onto, onto the core business.
And in, in those instances they don't want the founders to stay in at all.
So it's, it really does depend.
We just need to get as many buyers looking at the opportunities as possible.
And if it does affect, what it means is some buyers don't like it and so they would just offer less for it.
And if we've only got offers from buyers that don't like it, then maybe they'll come in a bit lower.
So I mean it has to be expected.
But we will go to market at the best price we can get for the business.
And obviously we're, we're here to negotiate with those buyers and, and push the price up.
Really the key thing is, is to get multiple buyers at the table at the same time.
Awesome.
Yeah, I mean, I'm guessing it's, I mean I'm probably biased, but I, I think in our micro niche like the, the agency, the name, the brand is very well known.
So I'm guessing there will be some interest if, I mean obviously people know this micro niche a bit, this vertical of advertising.
So that's perfect.
In one last thing regarding, obviously I'm guessing we're gonna need support by a lawyer at some point, especially towards the end.
Is that something you guys can help us with, with referrals or how would that look like?
Yeah, sure, we can, we can refer.
We've got a bunch of lawyers that we've seen fairly regularly over the years that we, that we do make referrals to.
So we can help you.
That, I mean we, yeah, we, we don't offer any legal advice ourselves.
So you will need to find some, somebody to disport you during that last bit.
But it's very important as well you don't hire the lawyer too early because they start to want to be involved in absolutely everything.
It just really pushes the costs up.
And to Bill, I guess from, from earlier, which is not.
Yeah, of course.
Yeah, they just, but, but also they mess up the negotiation because they scare the buyers and it just becomes really difficult to get a deal done.
What we want to do is have you and the buyer just talking and, and getting the deal just fleshed out before, before the, the legal thing.
We want, want a contract from the buyer on the table and, and then take that to your, to your lawyer.
So.
Yeah, cool.
Yeah, that's correct.
Yeah, we can help with that at the right time there.
That's perfect.
Cool.
So regarding the next steps, you sent us the engagement letter.
I'm guessing that's the next step then providing you with the financials.
Yeah.
So next steps is sign the engagement letter and then we'll get you onboarded so we can sort out invoicing and getting all of the payments moving.
And then yes, we'll have a kickoff call.
So it'll be maybe myself or one of our team on the deal side.

And it's just a deep dive then Questionnaire, really all of the stuff that we need to know about the business so that we can put together the marketing materials and then we start producing that, which is the teaser, the im, the listing.
And there will be some financial requests during that process as well.
So we need your last 3 years financials plus the current management accounts with your budget or your targets for this year as well.
And then we can start putting together the valuation of the business.

And you'll have that as well as a document that will give you like three or four different ways of value in the business so that we can give you a range, a suggested range of what we think the business is going to, to sell for.
And you can ignore that as well and put the price as high as you want.
But you know, at the end of the day we're, we used to see what the offers look like.
So once we've been through your financials, we can kind of gauge what it's likely to be around.
Cool.
Yeah, that's perfect.
Yeah.
All right then.
I think everything sounds good.
You got anything?
No, no, no, no.
Okay, cool.
All right, so I'll set the engagement letter up and then you're saying that you'd like to sign it towards the end of the month?
Yeah, yeah.
So we can get the process started, I mean, from June.
That would be seven months if we consider June, I'm guessing.
But I mean, if it makes things easier on your side, we're happy to do that.
Yeah, well, like I say, there's been a lot of interest this last two or three weeks.
It really seems to be to be picking up.
So if we can, if we can ride some of that wave, then the earlier the better.
So.
All right, I'll get that engagement letter set up and dated for maybe two weeks from today and then we're close to the end of the month and get started.
Awesome.
Sounds great.
Last thing, just out of curiosity, so you guys work with sellers and buyers in the agency space.
So I'm guessing you have some sort of a list of potential buyers, sellers and so on.
Is that list mainly US based on or anything else?
So it is mainly US based us, UK mainly, but we've also done a lot of work throughout Europe and the Middle east, particularly Germany is a really big market.
So we do have a completely international list of buyers.
Australia, Canada.
I would say that most of the deals do end up getting done with an American company.
They just have the most money and are buying the most marketing agencies.
But.
But it tends to be that they are just listed.
You know, sometimes they're listed in the U.S.
or they're based in the U.S.
but the founder actually lives in another country or is.
Or is somewhere else.
So makes sense across the globe in those instances.
Yeah, I keep out again.
No, that's fine.
There you go.
Makes perfect sense.
Cool.
Yeah.
My only concern was the.
I mean the current macro situation that like I thought could be scary for some of the potential buyers, but agencies are kinda easy to pivot or easy, like are flexible as a business model.
So I'm guessing if you have to buy, you'd rather buy something similar.
Yeah, if you've got to buy, you've got to buy.
Even if the dollar is.
Is down a little bit.
Again, they could be storing currencies abroad.
They might have some Euro currencies or something else going on.
But yeah, I mean, that is a fair point.
But like I say, the last two or three weeks we've seen a massive uptick and we actually have an American client that is looking for businesses in the UK today.
He's just called me up before this call so he's not put off, I should imagine.
I should imagine, generally speaking, like you say, people just have to get a transaction done.
The business has got to carry on growing and doing what it needs to do.
That makes sense.
Cool.
Perfect.
Awesome.
Thank you very much, Andy.
All right, good stuff.
Good to see you guys again.
Yeah, looking forward to working with you.
All right, cheers, guys.

summary.overview: In the recent Sales strategy and acquisition planning meeting between Alessio Cordeddu and Andy Day, key business updates were shared, including Alessio's two companies—99ads, focused on ad creation, and Creative Strategists, aimed at recruiting creative talent. The discussion covered the upcoming sale of 99ads, emphasizing an exclusivity clause limited to ad delivery, while confirming Francesco’s exit post-sale. Andy outlined the valuation insights and a typical six-month sales process, noting the impact of a founder's departure on valuation but reassured that growth—evidenced by a doubled EBITDA—poses a favorable selling condition. The team decided to expedite the sales process aiming for completion by year-end, with Alessio tasked to finalize financial documents and sign the engagement letter, while Andy will facilitate the process and provide necessary legal referrals as needed. The current market sentiment is optimistic, with a noted uptick in transaction activity despite broader economic concerns.
summary.short_summary: Alessio Cordeddu and Andy Day met to strategize on the sale of Alessio's company, 99ads, which specializes in ad creation. They confirmed that the sale will include an exclusivity clause related to ad delivery and noted Francesco's impending exit post-sale. Andy provided insights on valuation considerations, emphasizing that the founder's departure could impact the valuation. However, he reassured that the company's recent growth, highlighted by a doubled EBITDA, creates a positive environment for selling. The team agreed to accelerate the sales process with a target completion by year-end, assigning Alessio to finalize financial documents while Andy will assist with legal referrals. The market sentiment appears optimistic with increased transaction activity despite wider economic concerns.
